B04C001.summary: Janamejaya asks how his ancestors and Draupadi stayed hidden in Virata's city. Vaisampayana explains that after the asylum period Yudhishthira called his brothers together to choose a place for the thirteenth year of exile. Arjuna lists the neighboring kingdoms, and Yudhishthira settles on Matsya under King Virata, planning a disguise for each brother. The chapter sets up the whole plan of concealment that the rest of the Virata Parva follows.

scenes.B04C001S01: Janamejaya's question opens the section, and Yudhishthira, back from the asylum, asks his brothers to pick a hiding place; Arjuna names the kingdoms around the Kuru land.
scenes.B04C001S02: Yudhishthira chooses Matsya and its king Virata, then describes the disguise he will wear as a dice-playing courtier named Kanka, and asks what the others will do.

shots.B04C001S01H01: Heading that names the Pandava-Pravesa section.
shots.B04C001S01H02: Opening invocation to Narayana, Nara and Saraswati, and a call to utter the word Jaya.
shots.B04C001S01H03: Janamejaya asks how his ancestors lived unrecognized in Virata's city while fearing Duryodhana, and how Draupadi passed her days.
shots.B04C001S01H04: Vaisampayana says Yudhishthira returned from the asylum after gaining a boon from Dharma, returned a lost ritual item to a Brahmana, and told his brothers that the thirteenth year must now be spent hidden.
shots.B04C001S01H05: Arjuna says Dharma's boon lets them roam unseen, then lists the fertile neighboring kingdoms and asks which one Yudhishthira prefers.
shots.B04C001S02H01: Yudhishthira picks Virata's Matsya, calling its aged king virtuous and fond of the Pandavas, and says they will serve him in disguise.
shots.B04C001S02H02: Arjuna asks Yudhishthira what service he will take in Virata's court and how a king will bear such hardship.
shots.B04C001S02H03: Yudhishthira says he will appear as the Brahmana Kanka, a dice player and courtier who entertains the king with ivory pieces and dice. He asks Bhima what office he will fill.

B04C002.summary: Bhima chooses to pass as the cook Vallava and plans to show his strength through wrestling and fights with wild animals, while sparing the lives of his opponents. Yudhishthira then names Arjuna's famous feats at length and asks what role the great archer will take. Arjuna answers that he will appear as a eunuch named Vrihannala who teaches dance and song to the palace women, hiding his bowstring scars under bangles.

scenes.B04C002S01: Bhima describes his cover as a cook and wrestler, Yudhishthira praises Arjuna and asks his role, and Arjuna answers with his own disguise as Vrihannala.

shots.B04C002S01H01: Bhima says he will present himself as the cook Vallava, boast of his skill with curries and loads of wood, and take on wrestlers and beasts without killing them.
shots.B04C002S01H02: Yudhishthira asks what role Arjuna will take, and lists his deeds and his powers in a long run of comparisons that praise him as the finest of warriors.
shots.B04C002S01H03: Arjuna says he will pass as a eunuch named Vrihannala, cover his scarred arms with bangles, and teach singing and dance to the women, claiming to be Draupadi's former attendant.
shots.B04C002S01H04: Vaisampayana says Arjuna fell silent and the king turned to another brother.

B04C003.summary: Yudhishthira asks Nakula and Sahadeva what roles they will take, and both choose work with animals. Nakula will look after horses under the name Granthika, and Sahadeva will tend cattle as Tantripala. Yudhishthira then worries about Draupadi, who has never done ordinary work, and Draupadi proposes to serve Queen Sudeshna as a hairdresser. Yudhishthira agrees but warns her to guard her conduct so that wicked men are not drawn to her.

scenes.B04C003S01: Nakula and Sahadeva each name the work they will do in disguise, and Yudhishthira voices his concern for Draupadi.
scenes.B04C003S02: Draupadi offers to pass as a hairdresser serving the queen, and Yudhishthira cautions her about her conduct.

shots.B04C003S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Nakula what work he will take up in the king's realm.
shots.B04C003S01H02: Nakula says he will be keeper of Virata's horses under the name Granthika, and cites his skill in training horses and his old service to Yudhishthira.
shots.B04C003S01H03: Yudhishthira asks Sahadeva how he will carry himself and what disguise he will use.
shots.B04C003S01H04: Sahadeva says he will tend the king's cows under the name Tantripala, citing his skill with cattle, bulls and their markings.
shots.B04C003S01H05: Yudhishthira grieves over Draupadi, who is young, delicate and used only to garlands and fine robes, and asks what work she will do.
shots.B04C003S02H01: Draupadi offers to pass as a Sairindhri, a hairdresser who serves in other households, and to attend Queen Sudeshna under a cover story.
shots.B04C003S02H02: Yudhishthira agrees with her plan but warns her, given her noble birth and chastity, to behave so that wicked men are not drawn to look at her.

B04C004.summary: Yudhishthira sends his priest, cooks and charioteers to Drupada's realm, and Draupadi's maids to the Panchalas, while Indrasena and others head to Dwaravati. Dhaumya then gives a long set of rules for living in a king's household, covering how to speak, sit, and act around the ruler. Yudhishthira thanks him, and Dhaumya performs the departure rites and takes the sacred fires away. The brothers set out with Draupadi, and the household servants go their own separate ways.

scenes.B04C004S01: Yudhishthira arranges where the household goes, Dhaumya gives his counsel on royal service, and the brothers depart with Draupadi while the servants disperse.

shots.B04C004S01H01: Yudhishthira states the plan: priests and cooks go to Drupada's realm, Indrasena's group goes to Dwaravati, and Draupadi's maids say they do not know where the Pandavas went.
shots.B04C004S01H02: The brothers seek Dhaumya's advice, and he gives a long list of rules for serving a king, covering courtesy, speech, seating, dress, and loyalty.
shots.B04C004S01H03: Yudhishthira thanks Dhaumya for the counsel and asks him to make the arrangements for their departure and their safety.
shots.B04C004S01H04: Dhaumya performs the departure rites and offers prayers at the fires. The brothers leave with Draupadi, Dhaumya takes the sacred fires to the Panchalas, and Indrasena's group goes to the Yadavas.

B04C005.summary: The Pandavas, disguised as hunters, cross the Yamuna and enter Matsya, and Arjuna carries the weary Draupadi near the city. Yudhishthira worries that bearing their famous weapons into the city would reveal them, so Arjuna suggests hiding them in a Sami tree near a cemetery. The brothers hide the bows and weapons, hang up a corpse to keep people away, and take new names for the year. The chapter ends with them entering the city as planned.

scenes.B04C005S01: The brothers reach Matsya, carry Draupadi to the city's edge, hide their weapons in a Sami tree, and go in under new names.

shots.B04C005S01H01: The brothers leave the forest with swords and finger guards, cross the Yamuna and enter Matsya, and Draupadi notes they are still a distance from the city and asks for rest.
shots.B04C005S01H02: Yudhishthira tells Arjuna to carry Draupadi, since the city is just beyond the forest.
shots.B04C005S01H03: Arjuna lifts Draupadi and sets her down near the city. Yudhishthira asks where to leave the weapons, since bringing the famous bow inside could expose them and end the disguise.
shots.B04C005S01H04: Arjuna suggests a huge Sami tree near a cemetery in a remote forest, where no one is likely to see them hide their arms.
shots.B04C005S01H05: The brothers unstring their bows and hide them and their weapons in the tree, hang a corpse nearby to keep people away, and claim it is their mother. They take the names Jaya, Jayanta, Vijaya, Jayatsena and Jayadvala, and enter the city to pass the thirteenth year.

B04C006.summary: On the way to Virata's city, Yudhishthira prays to the goddess Durga, naming her many forms and asking for protection. The goddess appears and promises that the Pandavas will win the war and regain the earth. She also says that the Kurus' spies and the people of Matsya will fail to recognize them while they stay in Virata's city. The prayer gives the brothers divine cover for the disguised year.

scenes.B04C006S01: Yudhishthira prays to Durga, and the goddess appears to him and promises victory and concealment.

shots.B04C006S01H01: Yudhishthira, travelling toward Virata's city, prays to Durga, listing her many names and her powers over danger, and asks her for protection in his exile.
shots.B04C006S01H02: Durga appears and tells him he will defeat the Kauravas and recover his kingdom. She adds that those who recite her praises will be blessed, and that the Kurus' spies and the Matsyas will not recognize the brothers in Virata's city.

B04C007.summary: Yudhishthira arrives at Virata's court looking like a king in hiding, carrying golden dice. Virata cannot place him, and Yudhishthira presents himself as the Brahmana Kanka, a skilled dice player and former friend of Yudhishthira. Virata makes him a close companion with wide powers, and Yudhishthira asks for protection from quarrels over dice, which Virata grants. Kanka then lives in the court without being recognized.

scenes.B04C007S01: Yudhishthira enters Virata's court, Virata wonders who he is, and Yudhishthira introduces himself as Kanka and asks for a boon.
scenes.B04C007S02: Virata grants Kanka high status and privileges, and Kanka settles into the court unrecognized.

shots.B04C007S01H01: Yudhishthira appears in Virata's court with golden dice, looking like a king veiled in cloud. Virata asks his courtiers who this stranger is, noting he seems like a lord but has no retinue.
shots.B04C007S01H02: Yudhishthira asks to live near the king as a Brahmana who has lost his wealth. Virata welcomes him and asks his name, family and skills.
shots.B04C007S01H03: Yudhishthira gives his name as Kanka, a Brahmana of the Vaiyaghra family who is skilled at dice and once a friend of Yudhishthira.
shots.B04C007S01H04: Virata offers Kanka a share in ruling the Matsyas and says he likes skilled gamblers.
shots.B04C007S01H05: Yudhishthira asks for two boons: no quarrels with low people over dice, and no keeping of winnings by a loser.
shots.B04C007S02H01: Virata promises to punish anyone who displeases Kanka and makes him an equal friend, with access to clothes, food, the king's affairs and open doors.
shots.B04C007S02H02: Kanka lives happily and is well regarded in the court, and no one recognizes him.

B04C008.summary: Bhima enters Virata's court disguised as a cook, carrying a ladle, a spoon and a dark sword, and shining like the sun. Virata cannot tell who he is, but Bhima presents himself as the cook Vallava and offers to work in the kitchen. He adds that he is also a wrestler who fights lions and elephants, and Virata gives him charge of the royal kitchen. Bhima rises in the king's favour without being recognized.

scenes.B04C008S01: Bhima arrives as the cook Vallava, Virata is impressed and doubtful, and Bhima is appointed head of the kitchen.

shots.B04C008S01H01: Bhima comes into court holding cooking tools and a dark sword. Virata asks his people who this strong, handsome man is, then Bhima says he is Vallava, a cook who wants work in the kitchen.
shots.B04C008S01H02: Virata doubts that cooking is Bhima's true trade, and says he looks like a king.
shots.B04C008S01H03: Bhima says he is a cook who once served Yudhishthira, and also a wrestler who fights lions and elephants to amuse the king.
shots.B04C008S01H04: Virata grants his request and makes him superintendent of the kitchen, though he thinks the post is beneath him.
shots.B04C008S01H05: Bhima becomes the king's favourite in the kitchen and stays unrecognized by the other servants and the public.

B04C009.summary: Draupadi, dressed as a hairdresser in a single soiled cloth, wanders the city offering her services. Queen Sudeshna sees her from a terrace, is struck by her beauty, and asks who she really is. Draupadi says she serves as a hairdresser and claims that her five Gandharva husbands guard her, so no one can take her. Sudeshna takes her into the household on condition that she never touches another's leftovers or washes their feet.

scenes.B04C009S01: Draupadi wanders the city in disguise, is seen by Queen Sudeshna, and bargains her way into service with conditions.
scenes.B04C009S02: Draupadi begins living in the city, and no one can tell who she truly is.

shots.B04C009S01H01: Draupadi binds her hair in a braid, puts on a dirty single cloth, and wanders the city as a hairdresser. People find her too striking to be a common maid, and Queen Sudeshna notices her from a terrace.
shots.B04C009S01H02: Draupadi says she is a hairdresser who can also prepare perfumes and garlands, and says she served Satyabhama and Draupadi earlier under the name Malini.
shots.B04C009S01H03: Sudeshna praises Draupadi's beauty at length, guesses she may be a goddess or a celestial, and says she fears the king will be drawn to her.
shots.B04C009S01H04: Draupadi says her five Gandharva husbands protect her, and any man who tries to have her will die that very night.
shots.B04C009S01H05: Sudeshna agrees to take her into the household, on the condition that she never has to eat another's leftovers or wash another's feet.
shots.B04C009S02H01: Krishna (Draupadi), devoted to her husbands, begins to live in the city, and nobody learns who she really is.

B04C010.summary: Sahadeva, dressed as a cowherd, comes to the royal cattle pens, and Virata is struck by his bearing. He calls himself Arishtanemi, a Vaisya who once tended the Pandavas' herds and would serve no master but the king. When Virata doubts he is only a herdsman, Sahadeva describes his old work and his knowledge of cattle, and the king puts a hundred thousand cows under his care. Sahadeva lives there, and no one but his brothers recognize him.

scenes.B04C010S01: Virata meets the cowherd Sahadeva, questions him, and gives him charge of the royal herds.
scenes.B04C010S02: Sahadeva lives under Virata's protection, unrecognized.

shots.B04C010S01H01: Sahadeva arrives at the cowpens in a cowherd's dress and speech. Virata is amazed by his splendour and asks who he is and what work he wants.
shots.B04C010S01H02: Sahadeva says he is a Vaisya named Arishtanemi, who once tended the Kuru bulls, the sons of Pandu, and will serve no one else.
shots.B04C010S01H03: Virata doubts he is only a herdsman and asks him to name his true origin, skills and the pay he wants.
shots.B04C010S01H04: Sahadeva describes Yudhishthira's large herds, his old name Tantripala, his knowledge of cattle, their health and breeding, and the bulls whose markings are prized.
shots.B04C010S01H05: Virata gives him a hundred thousand cows with their herdsmen, placing all of them under his care.
shots.B04C010S02H01: Sahadeva lives happily under Virata's protection, and no one apart from his brothers recognizes him.

B04C011.summary: Arjuna appears at the court in women's ornaments and a braid, tall and commanding, so the king takes him for a noble and offers him a place. Arjuna calls himself Vrihannala, a singer and dancer, and asks to teach the princess Uttara. Virata agrees, but first has him tested in arts and examined by women, who confirm his condition. Arjuna then teaches music and dance in the women's quarters and goes unrecognized.

scenes.B04C011S01: Arjuna enters the court as Vrihannala, Virata offers him high status, Arjuna asks to teach Uttara, and he is tested and placed among the women of the palace.

shots.B04C011S01H01: Arjuna enters the court, huge and graceful, wearing women's ornaments and a braid. Virata asks where he came from and offers him a son's place or a share in ruling the Matsyas, saying he cannot be a eunuch.
shots.B04C011S01H02: Arjuna says he is skilled in dance, song and instruments, asks to be made dance teacher to princess Uttara, and gives his name as Vrihannala, without father or mother.
shots.B04C011S01H03: Virata agrees to assign him to his daughter and her companions, though he feels the post is beneath Arjuna.
shots.B04C011S01H04: Virata tests Vrihannala in dance and music and has women examine him. Finding the condition permanent, the king sends him to the women's apartments, where Arjuna teaches singing and music and lives unknown to anyone.

B04C012.summary: A fourth brother, Nakula, arrives at Virata's court and catches the king's eye by studying his horses. He offers his services as a horse trainer under the name Granthika, and Virata puts him in charge of all the royal horses and their keepers. Virata says he admires Nakula's bearing and wishes Yudhishthira were there. The chapter closes with the brothers living in Matsya, respected and still unrecognized.

scenes.B04C012S01: Nakula enters, impresses Virata with his knowledge of horses, and is appointed to manage the royal stables.

shots.B04C012S01H01: Nakula comes toward Virata, shining like the sun. Virata notices him studying the royal horses and, judging him a skilled horseman, orders him brought in.
shots.B04C012S01H02: Nakula presents himself as a horse trainer, names Yudhishthira as his former master, and lists his skill with breaking, correcting and healing horses. He says his name is Granthika.
shots.B04C012S01H03: Virata gives Nakula charge of all his horses, keepers and charioteers, and says his bearing makes him look like a king. He wonders how Yudhishthira is getting on in the forest, now that he has no servants.
shots.B04C012S01H04: The brothers live in Matsya as Virata's servants, well regarded, and no one recognizes them. The narrator notes they keep their pledge to pass the year in hiding.

B04C013.summary: Janamejaya asks what the Kuru princes did while living in disguise in Matsya. Vaisampayana describes how each brother earns a place: Yudhishthira wins at dice for the king, Bhima cooks and fights, Arjuna teaches the women, and the twins serve with horses and cattle. At a festival in the fourth month, Bhima defeats the champion wrestler Jimuta in a famous bout, and each brother is rewarded by Virata.

scenes.B04C013S01: Janamejaya asks what the brothers did, and Vaisampayana describes their hidden service, Bhima's wrestling victory at the festival, and the rewards they receive.

shots.B04C013S01H01: Heading that names the Samayapalana section.
shots.B04C013S01H02: Janamejaya asks what the mighty Kuru princes did while living disguised in Matsya.
shots.B04C013S01H03: Vaisampayana describes their hidden lives: Yudhishthira's dice winnings shared with his brothers, Bhima's meat sales, Arjuna's earnings from the women, Draupadi's care for the others, and a festival where Bhima kills the athlete Jimuta. The king rewards each of the brothers for their service.

B04C014.summary: After ten months, Kichaka, the commander of Virata's army and Sudeshna's brother, becomes obsessed with Draupadi when he sees her serving in the queen's rooms. He makes a long and lustful proposal, offering wealth and status, and Draupadi refuses. She reminds him that she is married and that her Gandharva husbands would kill him if he persisted. Kichaka does not give up and claims power over the realm, and Draupadi warns him again of the danger he is courting.

scenes.B04C014S01: Kichaka becomes infatuated with Draupadi, makes his advances through Sudeshna and then directly, and is repeatedly refused and warned.

shots.B04C014S01H01: Heading that names the Kichaka-badha section.
shots.B04C014S01H02: Vaisampayana says the brothers have passed ten months in disguise, and Draupadi serves Sudeshna in misery. Kichaka sees her, asks his sister Sudeshna about her, and then makes a lavish, lust-filled proposal to Draupadi with praise of her beauty. Draupadi refuses him, citing her position and her marriage, and asks him to respect moral law.
shots.B04C014S01H03: Kichaka, driven by desire, ignores her refusal and claims to be the true lord of the kingdom, offering her power and luxury. Draupadi warns him that her husbands are Gandharvas who will punish him, and that his attempt is hopeless and fatal.

B04C015.summary: Kichaka begs Sudeshna to help him win Draupadi, and Sudeshna arranges a plan: he is to prepare a feast of food and wine, and she will send the maid to fetch wine at his house. Draupadi objects, pointing out Kichaka's shamelessness and her vow to her husbands, but Sudeshna promises she will be safe. Draupadi prays to the Sun god, who sends a Rakshasa to guard her, while Kichaka rises in delight at her arrival.

scenes.B04C015S01: Kichaka asks Sudeshna for help, Sudeshna arranges a feast and sends Draupadi, and Draupadi prays for protection before entering Kichaka's presence.

shots.B04C015S01H01: Kichaka, rejected by Draupadi, begs Sudeshna to make the maid yield to him.
shots.B04C015S01H02: Sudeshna pities him and suggests he prepare food and wine for a festival, after which she will send the maid to bring wine and he can win her over in private.
shots.B04C015S01H03: Kichaka arranges fine food and drink. Sudeshna asks Draupadi to fetch wine from his house, and Draupadi objects, pointing to Kichaka's shameless nature and the vow she made on entering the palace. Sudeshna insists she will be safe and hands over a covered golden vessel, and Draupadi sets out after praying for protection.
shots.B04C015S01H04: Draupadi prays to the Sun god, who sends a Rakshasa to protect her unseen. When Kichaka sees her approaching like a frightened doe, he rises from his seat with a joy like that of a man reaching a boat to cross a river.

B04C016.summary: Kichaka seizes Draupadi in the court and kicks her in front of the assembled men, and a Rakshasa sent by Surya knocks him senseless. Bhima's anger rises, but Yudhishthira holds him back to protect their disguise, and Draupadi denounces Virata and his court for allowing the insult. The courtiers condemn Kichaka and praise her, and Yudhishthira sends her to Sudeshna's apartments, where she vows to see Kichaka dragged down.

scenes.B04C016S01: Kichaka tries to seize Draupadi and assaults her in the court, Bhima is held back by Yudhishthira, Draupadi rebukes the court, and she is sent away to Sudeshna.

shots.B04C016S01H01: Kichaka greets Draupadi, offers her jewels and wine, and when she says she has only come to fetch wine for the queen, he seizes her arm. Draupadi swears that he will end up dragged on the ground.
shots.B04C016S01H02: Kichaka grabs her garment and hair and kicks her before King Virata. A Rakshasa knocks him down, Bhima's rage is checked by Yudhishthira, and Draupadi cries out against the court.
shots.B04C016S01H03: Virata says he did not know what the quarrel was about. The courtiers, having learned the facts, condemn Kichaka and praise Draupadi's beauty.
shots.B04C016S01H04: Yudhishthira, sweating with anger, tells Draupadi to go to Sudeshna's apartments, and remarks that her Gandharva husbands are not coming to her aid.
shots.B04C016S01H05: Draupadi goes to Sudeshna in distress. The queen offers to have Kichaka killed, and Draupadi replies that those he has wronged will do it first.

B04C017.summary: Still stung by the insult, Draupadi bathes and thinks about how to get her revenge, deciding that only Bhima can do it. At night she goes to his quarters and finds him in the kitchen. She wakes him and asks how he can sleep while Kichaka lives, and Bhima asks her what she needs.

scenes.B04C017S01: Draupadi decides that Bhima must avenge her, goes to find him at night, and wakes him to demand action.

shots.B04C017S01H01: Draupadi bathes and, unable to find a remedy for her grief, thinks of Bhima as the only one who can carry out her revenge. She goes to his quarters at night and rouses him, asking how he can sleep while Kichaka is alive.
shots.B04C017S01H02: She finds Bhima in the kitchen, embraces and wakes him. He sits up, asks why she has come in such haste, and promises to help her if she tells him everything.

B04C018.summary: Draupadi answers Bhima by listing the humiliations she and the brothers have suffered. She blames Yudhishthira's loss at dice for their fall, and she contrasts his former splendour at Indraprastha with his present life as the courtier Kanka. Her speech is a sustained lament over the brothers' loss of status and her own grief.

scenes.B04C018S01: Draupadi lists her insults and blames Yudhishthira's gambling, lamenting his fall from the splendour of Indraprastha.

shots.B04C018S01H01: Draupadi tells Bhima of her many humiliations, including her dragging into the assembly, the insults of the forest, and Kichaka's assault. She blames Yudhishthira's gambling for their fall and laments how the once-honoured king now serves as the courtier Kanka.

B04C019.summary: Draupadi continues her plea to Bhima by describing how painfully each brother has been reduced to a humbling role. Bhima works as a cook and fights beasts for the women's amusement, Arjuna teaches dance and song as Vrihannala, Sahadeva tends cows, and Nakula handles the king's horses. She also reports that Sudeshna and her women mock her, suspecting her of favouring Bhima, and the chapter ends with her grief at how the brothers must live.

scenes.B04C019S01: Draupadi lists the humiliating roles of each brother, reports Sudeshna's mockery, and ends her grief-stricken plea.

shots.B04C019S01H01: Draupadi laments, at length, that Bhima serves as a cook and fights beasts before the court, that Arjuna teaches dance as a disguised eunuch, that Sahadeva tends cattle and Nakula trains horses, and that Sudeshna's women laugh at her and suspect her of favouring Bhima.

B04C020.summary: Draupadi tells Bhima how far the brothers have fallen: she serves Sudeshna, grinds sandal for others, and fears Virata, and her hands are now marked with calluses. She clings to hope that fortune will turn when the year ends, since fate rises and falls like a wheel. Bhima, moved by her grief, covers his face with her hands and weeps with her.

scenes.B04C020S01: Draupadi describes her humiliations and her hope for a turn of fortune, and Bhima weeps with her.

shots.B04C020S01H01: Draupadi describes her servitude under Sudeshna and her wait for the end of the exile, reasoning that fortune turns like a wheel. She lists her humiliations, including grinding sandal for others and showing Bhima her corn-marked hands.
shots.B04C020S01H02: Draupadi weeps and says the gods must be angry with her, since she is still alive when she should be dead.
shots.B04C020S01H03: Bhima weeps, holding her hands to his face and tears streaming down, as he begins to answer her.

B04C021.summary: Bhima answers Draupadi by cursing his own strength and Arjuna's bow for her hardship, and he admits he would have killed Kichaka if Yudhishthira had not restrained him with a look. Draupadi, though she does not blame Yudhishthira, repeats the story of Kichaka's pursuit, Sudeshna's jealousy, and the kick in the court, and she demands that Bhima kill him or she will take poison. Bhima consoles her, and then turns to his anger against Kichaka.

scenes.B04C021S01: Bhima voices his anger and regret, and Draupadi recounts Kichaka's pursuit and her refusals and demands revenge. Bhima then consoles her and turns his thoughts to Kichaka.

shots.B04C021S01H01: Bhima regrets his restraint and recalls the enemies he has not yet slain, urging Draupadi to hold her anger for her husbands' sake. Draupadi answers that she does not blame Yudhishthira, recounts Kichaka's pursuit, Sudeshna's jealousy and the kick, and says she will take poison if Kichaka is still alive when tomorrow's sun rises.
shots.B04C021S01H02: Draupadi hides her tear-streaked face against Bhima's chest, and he comforts her and wipes her face. He then licks his lips in anger at the thought of Kichaka and speaks to her.

B04C022.summary: Bhima and Draupadi plot to lure Kichaka to the empty dance hall, where Bhima waits for him at night. Kichaka arrives expecting Draupadi, boasts of his wealth and beauty, and Bhima overpowers and kills him after a long wrestling struggle. The Kichakas then try to burn Draupadi on Kichaka's pyre, but Bhima uproots a tree and kills their kin, and the total slain reaches 106 with Kichaka. The episode ends Draupadi's persecution and makes the court marvel at the feat.

scenes.B04C022S01: Bhima and Draupadi set the trap, and Kichaka comes to the dance hall at night, where Bhima receives him.
scenes.B04C022S02: Bhima and Kichaka wrestle, Bhima kills him, and the Kichakas' kin prepare to burn Draupadi with the body until Bhima comes to her rescue, uprooting a tree and killing 105 of them.
scenes.B04C022S03: The narrator tallies the dead and the wonder of the onlookers.

shots.B04C022S01H01: Bhima tells Draupadi he will kill Kichaka, and describes the dance hall where the girls dance by day and go home at night. He asks her to arrange the meeting so no one sees her.
shots.B04C022S01H02: Kichaka comes to Draupadi, boasts that he is the real power in Matsya, and offers her wealth and servants if she yields to him. Draupadi sets the condition that the meeting stay secret, and sends him to the dance hall at night.
shots.B04C022S01H03: Kichaka, delighted, dresses and adorns himself while Draupadi goes to Bhima in the kitchen and reports the plan, urging him to kill Kichaka in the hall.
shots.B04C022S01H04: Bhima welcomes the news and swears on truth and his brothers that he will kill Kichaka and anyone who defends him. He tells Draupadi he will do it that same night, unseen by others.
shots.B04C022S01H05: Bhima waits in the dark hall like a lion for its prey. Kichaka enters, boasts of the gifts he has given the woman, and Bhima answers with mocking flattery of Kichaka's skills.
shots.B04C022S02H01: Bhima seizes Kichaka by the hair and they wrestle at length, with Bhima overpowering him and finally crushing him to death. Bhima then shows the body to Draupadi, and she has the dance-hall guards told that Gandharvas slew him.
shots.B04C022S02H02: Heading that marks a new section.
shots.B04C022S02H03: Kichaka's kinsmen wail over his body and, with Virata's consent, seize Draupadi and carry her toward the cemetery to be burned with him. She calls on her husbands by their names for help.
shots.B04C022S02H04: Bhima hears her cries, tells her she need no longer fear the Sutas, and rises from his bed.
shots.B04C022S02H05: Bhima leaves the palace by a back way, climbs a wall, and uproots a huge tree to carry against the Sutas. He drives them off and kills a hundred and five of them, then frees Draupadi and comforts her before returning to the kitchen by another route.
shots.B04C022S03H01: The dead lie scattered like fallen trees after a storm. With Kichaka himself, the number slain comes to a hundred and six, and onlookers are left astonished.

B04C023.summary: Citizens report the deaths of the Sutas to Virata, who orders the Kichakas cremated and sends a message to Draupadi through Sudeshna, saying she may go wherever she likes. Draupadi returns to the city, where people flee in fear, and she greets Bhima as a Gandharva who saved her. In the dance hall she meets Arjuna and the princesses, and when Sudeshna brings the king's message she asks for thirteen more days before she leaves.

scenes.B04C023S01: Virata hears the report, sends his message to Draupadi through Sudeshna, Draupadi returns to the city and greets Arjuna and the princesses, and she asks for thirteen more days.

shots.B04C023S01H01: Citizens tell Virata that the Sutas were slain by Gandharvas and warn that Draupadi endangers his realm. Virata orders the Kichakas burned with rich honours and asks Sudeshna to tell Draupadi she may go wherever she pleases, since he dares not speak to her directly.
shots.B04C023S01H02: Freed from her captors, Draupadi washes and walks back to the city, where people flee in fear of the Gandharvas. At the kitchen gate she sees Bhima and thanks the Gandharva who rescued her, and Bhima replies in riddles that those who once answered to Kichaka are now free.
shots.B04C023S01H03: Draupadi finds Arjuna instructing Virata's daughters in dance. The girls congratulate her on her escape, and Vrihannala asks how it happened, while Draupadi answers with bitter mockery and Arjuna answers that he has sorrows of his own.
shots.B04C023S01H04: Draupadi goes to Sudeshna, who passes on the king's word that she may go wherever she likes. Draupadi asks to remain in the king's service for thirteen more days, since then the Gandharvas will take her away.

B04C024.summary: News of Kichaka's killing spreads through the provinces, and people praise both Vallava and the dead commander as warriors. Duryodhana's spies return from their search having found no trace of the Pandavas, and they report that the charioteers reached Dwaravati without them. They tell Duryodhana that Kichaka's death by Gandharvas gives the Kauravas a fresh opportunity against Virata.

scenes.B04C024S01: Word of Kichaka's killing spreads, and Duryodhana's spies report their failed search and the chance that Kichaka's death opens up.

shots.B04C024S01H01: People across the provinces talk of Kichaka's slaying by the Gandharvas and of his reputation as a wicked oppressor, while Vallava is praised for courage.
shots.B04C024S01H02: The spies return to Duryodhana's court and report that they found no trace of the Pandavas, that the charioteers returned to Dwaravati without them, and that Kichaka and his brothers are dead, which they call good news for the Kauravas.

B04C025.summary: Duryodhana reflects that most of the hidden year is over and orders his courtiers to find the Pandavas before they return. Karna urges more spies, sent in disguise to every likely place. Duhsasana doubts the search will succeed and suggests the brothers may have perished or fled abroad, but he advises Duryodhana to act with energy.

scenes.B04C025S01: Duryodhana orders a renewed search, Karna urges wider spying, and Duhsasana doubts the brothers can be found.

shots.B04C025S01H01: Heading that names the Go-harana section.
shots.B04C025S01H02: Duryodhana notes most of the thirteenth year has passed and asks his men to find the brothers before the year ends. Karna urges more and better spies in many places, and Duhsasana doubts they will be found and urges Duryodhana to put his mind at rest.

B04C026.summary: Drona argues that the Pandavas cannot be destroyed, since they are brave, disciplined and loyal to Yudhishthira's virtue and wisdom. He advises a renewed search using Brahmanas, Charanas and ascetics who know the brothers.

scenes.B04C026S01: Drona defends the Pandavas' virtue and recommends a new search by holy men.

shots.B04C026S01H01: Drona says the Pandavas will never perish, praises their loyalty to Yudhishthira and his virtue, and urges that the search be renewed with Brahmanas, Charanas and ascetics.

B04C027.summary: Bhishma agrees with Drona about the Pandavas' virtue but advises against using spies to hunt them now. He describes at length how the land where Yudhishthira dwells would prosper, with good rain, harvests, cattle and honest people. He ends by urging Duryodhana to act wisely and honestly.

scenes.B04C027S01: Bhishma supports Drona's praise of the Pandavas, counsels against spying, and describes the prosperity of the land where Yudhishthira hides.

shots.B04C027S01H01: Bhishma approves Drona's words, praises the Pandavas' virtue and discipline, and advises against using spies to expose them now. He describes the prosperity of any land where Yudhishthira lives, and urges Duryodhana to act wisely and honestly.

B04C028.summary: Kripa agrees with Bhishma but says Duryodhana should not ignore the Pandavas, since even a minor foe must be watched. He urges Duryodhana to track them by spies, learn his own strength and that of his allies, and build up his army and treasury before the brothers return. He then advises him to choose between fighting and making a treaty.

scenes.B04C028S01: Kripa agrees with Bhishma but urges Duryodhana to watch the Pandavas, build his strength, and prepare for war or treaty.

shots.B04C028S01H01: Kripa agrees with Bhishma but advises Duryodhana to keep tracking the brothers through spies, weigh his own strength and allies, and expand his army and treasury before the Pandavas return.

B04C029.summary: Susarman, the Trigarta king whom Kichaka had repeatedly defeated, urges Duryodhana to invade Virata's kingdom now that Kichaka is dead. Karna supports the plan and says the Pandavas are either gone or dead. Duryodhana orders the Trigartas to strike first at Virata's cattle, with the Kauravas following a day later, and both armies move out.

scenes.B04C029S01: Susarman urges an invasion, Karna supports it, and Duryodhana orders a two-pronged raid on Virata's cattle.

shots.B04C029S01H01: Susarman, humiliated by Kichaka, urges an invasion of Virata's kingdom to seize his gems, wealth and cattle. Karna approves, saying the sons of Pandu are either dead or gone and that the raid will be profitable.
shots.B04C029S01H02: Duryodhana orders his brother Duhsasana to muster the forces. The Trigartas are to go first and seize the cowherds' cattle, and the Kauravas will follow in two divisions.
shots.B04C029S01H03: The Trigartas march south-east, and Susarman sets out on the seventh day of the dark fortnight. The next day the Kauravas begin seizing cattle by thousands.

B04C030.summary: The Pandavas complete their year in disguise, and Virata, relying on them after Kichaka's death, learns that Susarman has seized thousands of his cattle. A herdsman brings the news to court, and Virata arms his brothers and sons, and orders chariots and armour for the disguised Pandavas. The brothers ride out with the king's army, which marches after the cattle tracks.

scenes.B04C030S01: The Trigartas seize Virata's cattle, the king arms his forces, and the brothers ride out with the army.

shots.B04C030S01H01: With the exile complete, a herdsman tells Virata the Trigartas are seizing his cattle. The king arms his brothers and sons in splendid armour, orders chariots and mail for the disguised Pandavas by their assumed names, and the brothers ride out with the army of Matsya.

B04C031.summary: The Matsyas and the Trigartas clash at sunset in a huge battle that leaves the field strewn with dead and wounded men. Satanika and Visalaksha break deep into the Trigarta ranks, and Virata duels with Susarman, wounding him and being wounded in turn. Dust and arrows hide the field, and the fighting stops at nightfall with neither side the clear winner.

scenes.B04C031S01: The Matsyas and Trigartas fight a fierce battle at sunset, and the king duels with Susarman until darkness falls.

shots.B04C031S01H01: The Matsya army marches out and meets the Trigartas in a battle that rages from afternoon into dusk. Heads, limbs and bodies cover the field, and by nightfall neither side has routed the other, while the king duels Susarman and both are wounded.

B04C032.summary: After a pause in the night fighting, the moon rises and the battle resumes, and Susarman and his brother seize Virata and carry him off. Yudhishthira urges Bhima to rescue the king, and Bhima, who wants to uproot a tree as a weapon, is told to use ordinary arms so that he is not recognized. Bhima routs the Trigartas, binds Susarman, and Yudhishthira then frees him on the condition that he declare himself a slave in every assembly.

scenes.B04C032S01: Virata is captured, Yudhishthira urges Bhima to rescue him, Bhima routs the Trigartas and binds Susarman, and Yudhishthira frees the captive.

shots.B04C032S01H01: The fighting resumes under the moon, and Susarman and his brother capture Virata and drive him away. Yudhishthira tells Bhima that the brothers owe the king a debt and must rescue him.
shots.B04C032S01H02: Bhima prepares to uproot a huge tree as a weapon, but Yudhishthira forbids such superhuman feats, warning that people would recognize him, and tells him to use an ordinary weapon.
shots.B04C032S01H03: Bhima routs the Trigarta cars and soldiers, while the brothers slay many hundreds and thousands of enemies. Bhima seizes and kicks Susarman, binds him and brings him to Yudhishthira, who orders him freed after Bhima sets the humbling condition that Susarman call himself a slave.

B04C033.summary: Shamed by his defeat, Susarman goes home, and Virata thanks the Pandavas with gems, wealth and an offer of rule over the Matsyas. Yudhishthira answers graciously, and Virata sends messengers to proclaim his victory in the city, and the proclamation is made at sunrise.

scenes.B04C033S01: Susarman is released, Virata rewards the Pandavas and offers them rule, and the city is told of the victory.

shots.B04C033S01H01: Susarman, humiliated, bows his head, is released, and departs. Virata rewards the Pandavas with gems, damsels and wealth, and tells them they may live happily and become lords of the Matsyas.
shots.B04C033S01H02: Yudhishthira thanks Virata, and Virata offers him the sovereignty of the Matsyas, gems, kine and gold. Yudhishthira asks him to send messengers to proclaim the victory, and Virata has them announce it at the city gates at sunrise.

B04C034.summary: While Virata is away chasing the Trigartas, Duryodhana's army invades Matsya, drives off the cowherds, and seizes sixty thousand cows. A chief cowherd rushes to the city and urges Virata's son Bhuminjaya to ride out and win back the herds, comparing his bow to a lute. The prince then begins to boast among the women of the palace.

scenes.B04C034S01: The Kauravas raid Virata's cattle, a cowherd reports to the prince, and the prince is urged to go out and fight.

shots.B04C034S01H01: Duryodhana, Karna, Drona, Bhishma and other warriors invade Matsya, drive off the cowherds and seize sixty thousand cows. The chief cowherd reaches the city, tells Bhuminjaya what has happened, and urges him to rescue the herds, comparing the bow to a lute.
shots.B04C034S01H02: Hearing this in front of the women, the prince boasts of his own courage and skill.

B04C035.summary: Uttara, Virata's son, laments that his charioteer died in the earlier battle and says he could recover the cattle if he had a skilled driver. Arjuna, speaking privately to Draupadi, suggests that Vrihannala, once Arjuna's charioteer, be asked. Draupadi reluctantly vouches for Vrihannala's skill, but Uttara doubts a eunuch can drive, so Draupadi says Vrihannala will obey Uttara's younger sister, and the sister is sent to fetch him from the dance hall.

scenes.B04C035S01: Uttara calls for a charioteer, Arjuna's plan is relayed through Draupadi, and Draupadi and Uttara debate whether Vrihannala can take the role.
scenes.B04C035S02: Uttara sends his sister to the dance hall to fetch Vrihannala.

shots.B04C035S01H01: Uttara declares he would ride after the cattle at once if he had a skilled charioteer, since his own was slain in the battle. He boasts that he would drive into the Kuru army and defeat even its mightiest warriors.
shots.B04C035S01H02: Arjuna speaks privately to Draupadi and asks her to tell Uttara that Vrihannala was once Arjuna's own charioteer.
shots.B04C035S01H03: Draupadi shyly tells Uttara that Vrihannala was Arjuna's disciple and a peerless driver, who once held the reins at Khandava and in the conquest of Khandavaprastha.
shots.B04C035S01H04: Uttara says Draupadi knows this youth and what he is, but he cannot himself ask Vrihannala to drive his horses.
shots.B04C035S01H05: Draupadi says Vrihannala will obey Uttara's younger sister, and if he agrees to drive, Uttara will win back the cattle.
shots.B04C035S02H01: Uttara sends his sister to the dance hall, where Arjuna is staying in disguise, to bring Vrihannala.

B04C036.summary: Virata's daughter, Uttara's sister, hurries to the dance hall and begs Arjuna, disguised as Vrihannala, to drive her brother's chariot against the Kurus. Arjuna first protests that he knows only singing, dancing and music, then pretends to be clumsy with the armour, and the maidens laugh until Uttara arms him himself. The women bless the chariot as it sets out, and Arjuna promises them cloth for their dolls if the battle goes well.

scenes.B04C036S01: Virata's daughter asks Arjuna to drive, Arjuna protests and pretends to be clumsy, Uttara arms him, and the women send them off with blessings.

shots.B04C036S01H01: Virata's daughter, richly adorned, hurries to the dance hall and greets Arjuna, asking why he is there and why she finds him in such a state of hurry.
shots.B04C036S01H02: She explains that her brother must fight the Kurus who have driven off the cattle and has no charioteer. She says the Sairindhri praised Vrihannala's skill, and she begs him to drive, saying she will die if he refuses.
shots.B04C036S01H03: Uttara orders Vrihannala to hold the reins and mount the chariot.
shots.B04C036S01H04: Arjuna pretends not to know how to put on the armour and the maidens burst out laughing. Uttara arms him himself, and Vrihannala promises the maidens cloth for their dolls if the Kurus are defeated.
shots.B04C036S01H05: The elderly women and Brahmanas walk around the chariot to bless the prince and his charioteer as they set out, wishing Vrihannala the kind of victory Arjuna won at Khandava.

B04C037.summary: Uttara drives toward the Kuru army, but when he sees its size and its great warriors he is terrified and begs Vrihannala to turn back. Vrihannala rebukes him, Uttara jumps down and runs, and Arjuna chases him, his braid and red garments flying, which amuses some Kuru soldiers. The Kurus wonder whether the runner could be Arjuna, Arjuna catches Uttara and calms him, and forces the frightened prince back into the chariot.

scenes.B04C037S01: Uttara drives toward the Kurus, panics at the sight of their army, flees, and is chased by Arjuna while the Kurus wonder who the charioteer is.
scenes.B04C037S02: Arjuna catches Uttara, reassures him, and lifts him back into the chariot.

shots.B04C037S01H01: Uttara orders Vrihannala to drive straight at the Kuru army, which he says has come to take the cattle. Arjuna drives on and the two see the enormous host, with its flags and great warriors.
shots.B04C037S01H02: Uttara, terrified, bewails his fate, saying his father has taken the army away and that he is only a boy with little training, and begs Vrihannala to stop the chariot.
shots.B04C037S01H03: Vrihannala mocks Uttara's fear, reminds him that he boasted before the women, and says he cannot return without the cattle.
shots.B04C037S01H04: Uttara replies that the Kurus may take the cattle and that people may laugh at him, but there is no need to fight.
shots.B04C037S01H05: Uttara throws down his bow and flees. Vrihannala rebukes him for running, and Arjuna leaps from the chariot and runs after him, his braid and red garments streaming, while some soldiers laugh. The Kurus argue over the identity of the figure and guess it may be Arjuna himself.
shots.B04C037S02H01: Arjuna overtakes Uttara and seizes him by the hair. Uttara begs him to turn back, promising a hundred gold coins and a chariot with ten elephants in return for his freedom.
shots.B04C037S02H02: Arjuna laughs, pulls the prince back to the chariot, and tells him to hold the reins while he fights. He reassures Uttara that he is a Kshatriya and a prince, then lifts him onto the car.
shots.B04C037S02H03: Heading that marks the next section.

B04C038.summary: The Kuru leaders see the figure in women's dress driving toward a Sami tree and fear that it is Arjuna. Drona reads a series of bad omens and identifies the driver by his many names and epithets, urging his men to stay on guard. Karna scoffs at Arjuna's worth, and Duryodhana says that if this is Arjuna the Pandavas will have to return to the forest, while a eunuch in disguise can be struck down; the Kuru elders applaud his courage.

scenes.B04C038S01: The Kuru leaders see the disguised driver and fear it is Arjuna, Drona reads omens, Karna and Duryodhana argue, and the elders applaud Duryodhana.

shots.B04C038S01H01: The Kuru warriors, Bhishma and Drona at their head, see the disguised charioteer carrying Uttara toward the Sami tree and suspect it is Arjuna. Drona reads omens of storms, dry clouds, restless weapons and frightened animals, and names Arjuna by his many epithets. Karna belittles Arjuna, and Duryodhana says the Pandavas would be sent back to the forest if it is him, or he will strike down a disguised eunuch.
shots.B04C038S01H02: Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and Drona's son applaud Duryodhana's manliness.

B04C039.summary: At the Sami tree, Arjuna tells Uttara, who is still inexperienced, to climb it and bring down the Pandavas' bows. He explains that the bows hidden there, including the Gandiva, are the only ones strong enough for his own use.

scenes.B04C039S01: Arjuna sends Uttara up the Sami tree to fetch the Pandavas' bows and names the Gandiva among them.

shots.B04C039S01H01: Arjuna, seeing Uttara is unpracticed in battle, tells him to climb the tree and take down the bows of the Pandavas, which are tied there along with their arrows, banners and armour. He names the Gandiva and explains that Uttara's own bows could not bear his strength.

B04C040.summary: Uttara objects to climbing the tree, since he has heard a corpse is tied in it and touching one would defile a prince. Arjuna assures him that there are only bows in the tree and no corpse, and Uttara climbs reluctantly. As he cuts the bindings and uncovers the weapons, they shine like the sun and frighten him, and he turns to Arjuna with a question.

scenes.B04C040S01: Uttara resists climbing the tree, Arjuna reassures him, and Uttara unwraps the bows and is struck by their brilliance.

shots.B04C040S01H01: Uttara says he has heard a corpse hangs in the tree, and that as a prince of the Kshatriya order he must not touch it.
shots.B04C040S01H02: Vrihannala assures him he will stay clean, since only bows hang in the tree and no corpse, and asks why he would make a prince do something shameful.
shots.B04C040S01H03: Uttara climbs the tree reluctantly, cuts away the wrappings and ropes, and finds the Gandiva with four other bows. Their brilliance and their snake-like shape frighten him, and he speaks to Arjuna as he holds them.

B04C041.summary: Holding the weapons, Uttara asks Vrihannala whose they are, one by one, naming the bows, arrows, quivers and swords with their golden and animal decorations. He is struck by their beauty and wonders aloud who could own such a collection.

scenes.B04C041S01: Uttara asks whose bows, arrows, quivers and swords these are, describing each in turn.

shots.B04C041S01H01: Uttara asks, one item after another, whose the golden-decorated bow, the arrows, the quivers and the various swords and scimitars are, and asks Vrihannala to tell him truly, since he marvels at them.

B04C042.summary: Arjuna, still disguised as Vrihannala, names the owners of each weapon. He identifies the Gandiva as his own, recounts how it passed through Shiva, Prajapati, Sakra, Soma and Varuna before he obtained it, and then assigns the other bows, arrows, quivers and swords to Yudhishthira, Bhima, Nakula and Sahadeva.

scenes.B04C042S01: Arjuna names the Gandiva as his own, traces its divine history, and assigns each of the other weapons to a brother.

shots.B04C042S01H01: Arjuna identifies the Gandiva as his own and traces its history through gods before it came to him from Varuna, then assigns the other bows, arrows, quivers and swords to Bhima, Yudhishthira, Nakula and Sahadeva, and gives the owner of each of the weapons described.

B04C043.summary: Uttara admires the weapons and asks where the Pandavas are now. Arjuna reveals that he is Arjuna and names his brothers' court disguises, along with the Draupadi who is serving as the Sairindhri. Uttara asks for proof, so Arjuna recites his ten names and explains the origin of several of them. Convinced, Uttara apologizes for his earlier doubts and welcomes him.

scenes.B04C043S01: Uttara asks where the Pandavas are, and Arjuna reveals his identity and the brothers' disguises, and Uttara asks for proof.
scenes.B04C043S02: Arjuna gives the meanings of his ten names, and Uttara apologizes and welcomes him.

shots.B04C043S01H01: Uttara admires the golden weapons and asks where the Pandavas have gone, since they lost their kingdom at dice and have not been heard of, and where Draupadi is.
shots.B04C043S01H02: Arjuna says he is Arjuna, and that Yudhishthira is the courtier, Bhima the cook, Nakula the horse-keeper and Sahadeva the cowherd. He adds that the Sairindhri is Draupadi, for whose sake the Kichakas were killed.
shots.B04C043S01H03: Uttara says he will believe it only if Arjuna can recite the ten names he has heard for him.
shots.B04C043S01H04: Arjuna lists his ten names: Arjuna, Phalguna, Jishnu, Kiritin, Svetavahana, Vibhatsu, Vijaya, Krishna, Savyasachin and Dhananjaya.
shots.B04C043S01H05: Uttara asks Arjuna to explain why he has each name, so he can check the answer against what he has heard.
shots.B04C043S02H01: Arjuna explains that Dhananjaya comes from his winning of wealth, Vijaya from his victories, Svetavahana from his white horses, Phalguna from his birth under a particular constellation, and Kiritin from the diadem Indra gave him. He also explains Vibhatsu, Savyasachin, Arjuna, Jishnu and Krishna, the last being a name his father gave him.
shots.B04C043S02H02: Uttara comes closer, greets Partha and begs pardon for his earlier ignorance, saying his fear is gone and his affection is great.

B04C044.summary: Uttara offers to drive Arjuna into the enemy ranks, and Arjuna promises to rout the Kurus, describing his chariot as a fortress with its own walls and gates. Arjuna explains that his eunuch disguise was a year-long vow kept at his elder brother's command. Uttara praises him and names the horses, and Arjuna prepares for battle, summons his weapons and sounds the Gandiva, which frightens Uttara, who fears the size of the Kuru army. Arjuna answers by recalling his past battles against gods and demons.

scenes.B04C044S01: Uttara offers his services, Arjuna describes his chariot as a fortress and explains his disguise as a vow.
scenes.B04C044S02: Uttara praises Arjuna and the horses, Arjuna readies himself and sounds the Gandiva, and he answers Uttara's fears.

shots.B04C044S01H01: Uttara offers to drive Arjuna wherever he wants to go in the enemy army.
shots.B04C044S01H02: Arjuna says he is pleased with the prince, promises to rout the foes, and asks him to tie the quivers to the chariot and take a golden sword.
shots.B04C044S01H03: Uttara climbs down and brings Arjuna's weapons. Arjuna says the chariot will be a fortress, with its pole and quiver as defenses, its banner a grand gate, and the bowstring as a catapult.
shots.B04C044S01H04: Uttara says he is no longer afraid, but wonders how a man so handsome and well marked could have lost his manhood, and asks if he is a god in disguise.
shots.B04C044S01H05: Arjuna explains that he is keeping a year-long eunuch vow because his elder brother asked him to, and that he is not truly a eunuch.
shots.B04C044S02H01: Uttara calls Arjuna the best of men, says he now has an ally, and praises the chariot and the four horses, naming each one and comparing them to famous steeds.
shots.B04C044S02H02: Arjuna removes his bracelets, puts on gloves, binds his hair, and summons his weapons, which greet him as their master. He sounds the Gandiva so loudly that the earth and sky shake, and when Uttara fears the Kuru numbers, Arjuna laughs and recalls his past battles against gods, demons and kings.

B04C045.summary: Arjuna circles the Sami tree, takes down the lion banner and raises his own ape banner, a celestial gift. When he sounds his conch the horses kneel and Uttara sinks down in fear, and Arjuna comforts him and sounds the conch again. Drona, watching from the Kuru side, reads the omens as signs of disaster and says the driver must be Savyasachin.

scenes.B04C045S01: Arjuna sets up his chariot and sounds the conch, Uttara is frightened, and Drona reads omens of a coming disaster.

shots.B04C045S01H01: Arjuna circles the Sami tree, takes down the lion banner, and raises his ape banner, a gift from Agni. He sounds his conch, the horses kneel, and Uttara sits down in fear, and Arjuna urges him not to be afraid.
shots.B04C045S01H02: Uttara says he has never heard such a conch, bow or banner, and that the noise and the sight have confused his senses and deafened him.
shots.B04C045S01H03: Arjuna tells Uttara to brace himself on the car and hold the reins firmly, because he will sound the conch again.
shots.B04C045S01H04: Arjuna sounds the conch again, and the sound shakes hills and mountains. Uttara clings to the chariot once more, and Arjuna comforts him again.
shots.B04C045S01H05: Drona says the thunder of the chariot and the darkened sky mean the driver is Savyasachin, and he lists bad omens among the Kuru ranks. He advises sending the cattle ahead and standing ready with the army in order.

B04C046.summary: Duryodhana argues that if the approaching warrior is Arjuna, the Pandavas have broken their pledge and must go back to the forest for twelve more years. He urges an immediate fight regardless of who the warrior is. Karna dismisses Drona's warnings as partiality to Arjuna and urges the army to stand firm.

scenes.B04C046S01: Duryodhana argues the Pandavas' year is not over and calls for battle, and Karna dismisses Drona's praise of Arjuna.

shots.B04C046S01H01: Duryodhana argues that the thirteenth year is not yet done, so if this is Arjuna the Pandavas must return to the forest for twelve years, and that the army must fight whoever it is. Karna then mocks Drona for praising Arjuna, says the preceptor is partial to the Pandavas, and urges the Kauravas to arrange their army and hold their ground.

B04C047.summary: Karna declares that he alone will stand against the approaching warrior, whether Arjuna or the Matsya king. He boasts at length that his arrows will cover and defeat Arjuna, that he has gained weapons from Jamadagni's son, and that he will hurl Arjuna from his chariot. He ends by saying the Kauravas may take the cattle or stay and watch.

scenes.B04C047S01: Karna boasts that he will defeat Arjuna and invites the Kauravas to watch.

shots.B04C047S01H01: Karna, seeing his comrades anxious, boasts that he will meet Arjuna with arrows that cover him like locusts, will break his chariot and strike down his ape banner, and that the Kauravas may take the cattle or stay and watch.

B04C048.summary: Kripa warns Karna against fighting Arjuna alone, reminding him that Arjuna has rescued the Kurus from the Gandharvas, defeated many enemies single-handed and mastered the weapons under Indra. Kripa says Karna is like a fool who tries to take the fangs of a snake or swim the ocean with a stone around his neck. He urges the six great warriors to stand together with their troops in ranks, rather than facing Arjuna alone.

scenes.B04C048S01: Kripa rebukes Karna's rashness, lists Arjuna's feats, and urges the Kuru warriors to fight together.

shots.B04C048S01H01: Kripa warns Karna that his rashness will lead to disaster, lists Arjuna's great deeds, and urges the six car-warriors to stand together in ranks instead of facing Arjuna alone.

B04C049.summary: Ashvatthaman rebukes Karna's boasting, reminding him that the cattle are not yet won and that true heroes keep quiet about their deeds. He condemns Duryodhana's gains from dice as dishonest and recalls the insult to Draupadi, and he warns that Arjuna will destroy the Kurus. He tells Karna to use the same dice-tricks that won Indraprastha, and says he himself will fight the Matsya king rather than Arjuna.

scenes.B04C049S01: Ashvatthaman answers Karna's boast with a sharp rebuke of Duryodhana's dishonest dice victory and a warning about Arjuna.

shots.B04C049S01H01: Ashvatthaman tells Karna that the cattle are not yet won, that real heroes do not boast, and that Duryodhana won his kingdom by dishonest dice, while the Pandavas acted honourably. He warns that Arjuna will destroy the Kurus, and declares that he himself will fight the Matsya king and not Arjuna.

B04C050.summary: Bhishma calls for unity, saying that Karna's boast was meant only to rally the army and that disunity among leaders is the worst calamity an army can suffer. Ashvatthaman replies that his father had praised Arjuna in anger, which is why he spoke. Duryodhana, with Karna, Kripa and Bhishma, urges Drona to forgive, and Drona agrees, asking that the army be arranged so that Arjuna cannot reach Duryodhana.

scenes.B04C050S01: Bhishma urges the leaders to unite, Ashvatthaman answers with his grievance, Duryodhana asks Drona to forgive, and Drona asks for battle arrangements.

shots.B04C050S01H01: Bhishma says Kripa and Drona's son are right, that Karna only spoke to raise courage, and that the leaders must forgive each other because disunity is the worst of calamities. Ashvatthaman answers that Bhishma's counsel was proper, but Drona had praised Arjuna in his anger, and an enemy's merits and a teacher's faults may both be spoken of.
shots.B04C050S01H02: Duryodhana asks the preceptor to forgive, so that peace can be restored.
shots.B04C050S01H03: Duryodhana, with Karna, Kripa and Bhishma, pacifies Drona.
shots.B04C050S01H04: Drona says he is now calmed by Bhishma's words, and asks that the army be placed so that Arjuna cannot reach Duryodhana or harm the troops. He says Arjuna has not revealed himself before the term ended, and that he will not pardon the raid on the cattle.

B04C051.summary: Bhishma works out the calendar and concludes that the Pandavas kept their promise, so Arjuna's appearance is lawful and battle cannot be avoided. Duryodhana refuses to return the kingdom and orders the preparations to go ahead. Bhishma advises the king to withdraw to the capital with a quarter of the army, send another quarter with the cattle, and fight with the rest, and then he arrays the troops around Drona, Ashvatthaman, Kripa and Karna.

scenes.B04C051S01: Bhishma calculates the exile's length and advises on the battle, Duryodhana refuses to yield, and Bhishma arrays the army.

shots.B04C051S01H01: Bhishma works out that the thirteen years are complete with time to spare, so the Pandavas kept their promise and Arjuna's appearance is lawful. He warns that the Pandavas will not give up their kingdom and that the Kurus must prepare for battle.
shots.B04C051S01H02: Duryodhana refuses to return the kingdom and orders every preparation for battle without delay.
shots.B04C051S01H03: Bhishma advises Duryodhana to return to the capital with a fourth of the army, have another fourth escort the cattle, and fight with the rest, while Bhishma, Drona, Karna, Ashvatthaman and Kripa face Arjuna.
shots.B04C051S01H04: Bhishma arranges the army: Drona in the centre, Ashvatthaman on the left, Kripa on the right, Karna in the van, and Bhishma himself guarding the rear.

B04C052.summary: Arjuna's chariot advances with a roar of its ape banner and the twang of the Gandiva, and Drona identifies Partha by his banner and bearing. Arjuna, suspecting that Duryodhana is retreating with the cattle by the southern road, asks Uttara to drive straight at the king. Kripa urges the Kuru warriors to counterattack, but Arjuna scatters their troops with arrows and conch-blasts, and the cattle turn back south.

scenes.B04C052S01: Arjuna's chariot advances, Drona recognizes him, Arjuna turns toward Duryodhana, and the Kuru troops are routed as the cattle turn back.

shots.B04C052S01H01: Arjuna's chariot rushes at the Kurus with its roaring ape banner, and Drona recognizes Partha by his banner, the twang of his bow and his bearing, comparing him to a sacrificial fire.
shots.B04C052S01H02: Arjuna asks Uttara to hold the horses where his arrows can reach the enemy, then says he will strike at Duryodhana, who must be retreating with the kine by the south.
shots.B04C052S01H03: Kripa, seeing Arjuna head for Duryodhana, urges his men to strike Arjuna's flank, since the cattle would be worthless if Duryodhana were lost. Arjuna shoots down the Kuru troops, blows his conch, and the cattle turn back along the southern road.

B04C053.summary: Having recovered the cattle, Arjuna turns back to face the Kuru army, driving Uttara straight into the thick of it. He routs several warriors, kills Satruntapa, and drives Vikarna off the field. Karna then challenges him, and after a long archery duel Arjuna wounds Karna in many places until Karna quits the battle.

scenes.B04C053S01: Arjuna turns back to fight, routs several Kuru warriors, and wounds Karna in a long duel that drives him from the field.

shots.B04C053S01H01: Arjuna, having recovered the cattle, turns back and drives Uttara into the Kuru army. He routs several Kuru warriors, kills Satruntapa, and drives off Vikarna, then meets Karna in a long archery duel in which he wounds him on the arms, head and body until Karna retreats.

B04C054.summary: After Karna flees, the other Kuru warriors attack Arjuna, but his arrows fill the sky and scatter their ranks, and the field is littered with dead elephants and men. Arjuna holds back from killing the defenceless and instead strikes from behind, and the battlefield turns red as evening comes on. Uttara asks where to drive, and Arjuna names each Kuru leader by his banner, from Kripa and Drona through Duryodhana and Karna to Bhishma, who should be approached last.

scenes.B04C054S01: Arjuna's onslaught scatters the Kuru army, and Arjuna names the Kuru leaders whom Uttara should approach.

shots.B04C054S01H01: Arjuna's arrows cover the field, and the Kuru ranks are shattered by his arrows, his dazzling bow and the roar of his conch. He refrains from killing the defenceless, strikes the army from behind, and keeps shooting until the sky turns red at evening, wounding Drona, Duryodhana, Bhishma, Karna and others.
shots.B04C054S01H02: Arjuna asks Uttara to drive to Kripa first, then to Drona, Ashvatthaman, Duryodhana and Karna by their banners, warning him to be careful near Karna, and to approach Bhishma last. Uttara obeys and turns the chariot toward Kripa.

B04C055.summary: Gods and heavenly beings come to watch the battle in their celestial chariots, led by Indra with his Vishvas and Maruts. The sky fills with divine light and fragrance, and the dust clears as Indra gazes at his son Arjuna and cannot look away.

scenes.B04C055S01: Gods, heavenly kings and sages gather in the sky to watch the battle, and Indra looks on at his son.

shots.B04C055S01H01: The Kuru ranks stand ready, and the gods arrive on celestial cars with Indra at their head to watch the battle between Arjuna and the Kurus. Divine perfumes spread over the field, the dust settles, and Indra cannot take his eyes off his son.

B04C056.summary: Arjuna sends Uttara against Kripa, and the two sound their conches in challenge. Kripa and Arjuna shoot at each other, but Arjuna cuts Kripa's bows as fast as Kripa can string them, slays his horses and driver, and wounds him in the breast. When Kripa hurls a mace it is turned back, and Kripa's men try to rescue him, but Uttara wheels the chariot in circles to hold them off until Kripa is carried away.

scenes.B04C056S01: Arjuna duels with Kripa, cutting down his weapons and car, and then Kripa is taken away by his men.

shots.B04C056S01H01: Arjuna orders Uttara to head toward Kripa's chariot, then sounds his conch Devadatta. Kripa answers with his own conch, and the two warriors begin shooting at each other.
shots.B04C056S01H02: Arjuna cuts down each new bow Kripa takes up, cuts off his armour, kills his horses and driver, and wounds him. When Kripa hurls a mace, Arjuna sends it back. Kripa's warriors surround Arjuna, but Uttara wheels the chariot in circles and holds them off while Kripa is led away.

B04C057.summary: Arjuna has Uttara drive toward Drona, praising the teacher's virtues and saying he will not strike unless he is struck first. Drona and Arjuna duel with celestial weapons, drawing admiration from the spectators on both sides. When Ashvatthaman charges at Arjuna, Arjuna turns to meet him, and Drona, wounded, withdraws from the field.

scenes.B04C057S01: Arjuna approaches Drona, respectfully declares his terms, and duels him until Drona withdraws wounded.

shots.B04C057S01H01: Arjuna tells Uttara to drive toward Drona's car with the golden altar banner, and praises Drona as the master of the Vedas, the celestial weapons and every virtue. He says he wishes to fight Drona.
shots.B04C057S01H02: Arjuna approaches with respect and promises not to strike unless struck first. The two shoot at each other with celestial weapons in a duel the spectators admire. When Ashvatthaman charges Arjuna, Arjuna turns toward him, leaving Drona to escape, wounded and with his armour and banner gone.

B04C058.summary: Ashvatthaman charges at Arjuna and the two fight fiercely while the sky is darkened by arrows. Ashvatthaman cuts the string of the Gandiva, and Arjuna restrings it and presses on, since Ashvatthaman's arrows soon run out. The Kurus cheer, and when Karna twangs his bow Arjuna turns to meet him.

scenes.B04C058S01: Ashvatthaman duels Arjuna, cuts the Gandiva's string, runs out of arrows, and Arjuna turns on Karna.

shots.B04C058S01H01: Ashvatthaman rushes at Arjuna and shoots in a fierce duel that darkens the sky. He cuts the Gandiva's string, but Arjuna restrings it and gains the advantage as Ashvatthaman's arrows run low, and then Karna twangs his bow and Arjuna turns toward him, enraged.

B04C059.summary: Arjuna confronts Karna and reproaches him for his boasting and for watching Draupadi be humiliated in the court. Karna answers that Arjuna's words exceed his deeds and that he had been held back by morality, and Arjuna answers that Karna fled when his brother was slain. The two begin a duel, in which Arjuna cuts Karna's bow and steeds and wounds him in the breast, and Karna flees northward while Arjuna and Uttara taunt him.

scenes.B04C059S01: Arjuna and Karna trade insults before their duel, Arjuna cuts Karna's weapons and wounds him, and Karna flees the field.

shots.B04C059S01H01: Arjuna challenges Karna to make good his boast before the Kurus, reproaching him for the insult to Draupadi and for the twelve years of suffering. Karna replies that Arjuna's words outrun his deeds and that Arjuna's forbearance was the result of his vow. Arjuna retorts that Karna ran from battle when his brother was slain, and calls him shameful.
shots.B04C059S01H02: The two duel with volleys of arrows. Arjuna cuts Karna's quiver strings, bow and steeds, pierces his breast, and Karna, who briefly loses consciousness from the wound, regains himself and flees northward while Arjuna and Uttara taunt him.

B04C060.summary: Uttara, overwhelmed by the sights, sounds and stench of battle, says he can no longer hold the reins. Arjuna reassures him and tells him to stay steady as a prince of Matsya's line, then boasts of his divine weapons and vows to break the Kuru host. He drives toward Bhishma, cuts down Bhishma's banner, and when four Kuru princes attack him he wounds Duhsasana and Vikarna and kills the horses of Dussaha and Vivingsati, driving them off.

scenes.B04C060S01: Uttara falters, Arjuna reassures him and boasts of his weapons, and Arjuna cuts Bhishma's banner and drives off the Kuru princes who attack him.

shots.B04C060S01H01: Uttara says he is overwhelmed by the horror of the battlefield, the stench of blood, the noise of conches and the twang of the Gandiva, and that he can no longer hold the reins. Arjuna tells him not to lose heart, as a prince of the Matsya line, and to stay on the car and steady the horses.
shots.B04C060S01H02: Arjuna orders Uttara to drive to Bhishma's division, boasting that he will cut Bhishma's bowstring and send the Kuru army fleeing, and he names the celestial gods who taught him his weapons.
shots.B04C060S01H03: Arjuna cuts off Bhishma's banner at the root. Duhsasana, Vikarna, Dussaha and Vivingsati then attack him. Arjuna wounds Duhsasana and Vikarna, who falls from his car, kills the horses of Dussaha and Vivingsati, and the brothers are carried away from the field.

B04C061.summary: The Kuru warriors attack Arjuna together from every side, but he covers them in arrows, and elephants, horses and men fall in heaps. Their courage broken, the Kuru troops flee in terror, and Arjuna's arrows create a river of blood across the battlefield.

scenes.B04C061S01: The Kuru warriors attack Arjuna together, Arjuna routs them with arrows, and the battlefield turns into a river of blood.

shots.B04C061S01H01: The Kuru warriors close in on Arjuna, but he covers them in clouds of arrows, breaks their armour and cuts down heaps of men, elephants and horses, while his bow seems to dance. The Kurus lose heart in front of Duryodhana and flee, and the field becomes a vast river of blood, heaped with corpses.

B04C062.summary: Bhishma, the grandsire, comes at Arjuna with his own bow and a shower of arrows, and the two fight with celestial weapons while the Kauravas and the gods watch. Arjuna cuts Bhishma's bow, umbrella and banner, and Bhishma repeatedly takes up a new bow and fights on. Indra and the Gandharva Chitrasena praise both warriors, but Arjuna finally wounds Bhishma in the breast, and Bhishma's charioteer carries him off the field.

scenes.B04C062S01: Bhishma and Arjuna duel with celestial and ordinary weapons, the gods praise them, and Arjuna wounds Bhishma and forces him from the field.

shots.B04C062S01H01: Bhishma comes at Arjuna with a golden bow and a shower of arrows, and blows his conch to challenge him. Arjuna cuts off Bhishma's umbrella and banner, and then his horses and drivers, and the two exchange celestial weapons while the Kauravas praise them both.
shots.B04C062S01H02: Arjuna cuts Bhishma's golden bow, and Bhishma takes up another and shoots back. The two trade volleys until no one can tell them apart, and the Gandharva Chitrasena praises both warriors to Indra.
shots.B04C062S01H03: Indra honours both with a shower of flowers. Arjuna cuts Bhishma's bow again and wounds him in the breast with ten arrows, and Bhishma leans on his car, senseless, until his driver takes him away.

B04C063.summary: Duryodhana attacks Arjuna and wounds him on the forehead, but Arjuna answers, slays Vikarna's elephant with a single iron arrow, and wounds Duryodhana in the breast. The Kuru army breaks and flees, and Duryodhana turns to run as well. Arjuna shames him for running away, reminds him of his royal duty, and urges him to turn back and fight.

scenes.B04C063S01: Duryodhana and Arjuna trade wounds, Arjuna kills Vikarna's elephant, and Arjuna shames Duryodhana as he flees.

shots.B04C063S01H01: Duryodhana attacks Arjuna, wounds him on the forehead, and the two exchange wounds. Arjuna kills Vikarna's huge elephant with an iron arrow, wounds Duryodhana in the breast, and the Kuru warriors flee. Duryodhana turns his chariot to run, and Arjuna shames him, saying a king should not run, and tells him to turn back and show his face.

B04C064.summary: Stung by Arjuna's taunts, Duryodhana turns his chariot back, and Karna, Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and the others close in to protect him. Arjuna stuns the whole Kuru army with a celestial weapon and his conch, then has Uttara strip the fallen warriors of their garments. Bhishma alone recovers and advises Duryodhana to go home, and Arjuna breaks Duryodhana's jewelled crown, salutes the elders, and sounds his conch as the Kurus depart.

scenes.B04C064S01: The Kurus rally against Arjuna, Arjuna stuns them with a weapon and his conch, Bhishma counsels Duryodhana to leave, and Arjuna salutes the elders and sounds his conch.

shots.B04C064S01H01: Duryodhana turns back, and Karna, Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Vivingsati, Duhsasana and others advance to surround Arjuna. Arjuna releases a celestial weapon called Sanmohana and blows his conch, which stuns the whole army so that the warriors drop their bows. Arjuna has Uttara take the garments of the fallen, and Bhishma, who is not stunned, attacks and fights him until his steeds are killed.
shots.B04C064S01H02: Bhishma tells Duryodhana that his lapse was shameful and that he should go home to Hastinapura, since Arjuna will not kill for the sake of cowardice. Arjuna then salutes the elders and breaks Duryodhana's jewelled crown with an arrow, and sounds his conch as the Kurus depart, while the gods leave pleased with his feats.

B04C065.summary: Arjuna drives the recovered cattle back toward Virata's city, and a band of Kuru soldiers who had fled into the forest comes out and begs for mercy. Arjuna spares them and tells Uttara to claim the victory himself rather than praise the Pandavas, which might frighten Virata into hiding. Arjuna returns the weapons and the banner to the Sami tree, enters the city as Vrihannala, and sends word ahead, and the prince and his companions retrieve their garments from the tree before entering.

scenes.B04C065S01: Arjuna spares a band of Kuru soldiers who beg for mercy, tells Uttara to take the credit, and returns to the Sami tree to restore the weapons.
scenes.B04C065S02: Arjuna asks Uttara to send news ahead of their return, and the party collects their garments and enters the city.

shots.B04C065S01H01: Arjuna drives the recovered cattle home, and a band of frightened Kuru soldiers comes out of the forest, hands joined and hair dishevelled, and calls itself his slave.
shots.B04C065S01H02: Arjuna tells them to go in peace, that he will not kill the afflicted, and gives them his protection.
shots.B04C065S01H03: The soldiers bless Arjuna, and the Kurus cannot match him as he goes back toward Virata's city. Arjuna tells Uttara not to reveal the Pandavas, and to claim the victory himself, since the king might hide in fear if he heard their praise.
shots.B04C065S01H04: Uttara says he could never perform such a feat, and promises not to reveal Arjuna's identity unless asked.
shots.B04C065S01H05: Arjuna returns to the Sami tree, the ape banner dissolves, and Uttara's lion banner is raised again. The weapons are restored to the car, and Arjuna takes up the reins once more, binds his hair in a braid, and enters the city as Vrihannala, Uttara's driver.
shots.B04C065S02H01: On the way, Arjuna asks Uttara to send cowherds ahead with the good news, so that the city can prepare to receive them.
shots.B04C065S02H02: Uttara sends messengers to proclaim the king's victory. The Matsya and Bharata princes return to the Sami tree, dress in the garments they left there, and ride back to the city with Vrihannala as driver.

B04C066.summary: Virata returns in triumph with the Pandavas and learns that Uttara has gone out alone with only Vrihannala as driver. He sends a force after him, but Yudhishthira predicts victory, and news of the win arrives. Virata rejoices and turns to a game of dice with Kanka, but when Yudhishthira again praises Vrihannala the king strikes him with a die, drawing blood that Draupadi catches, and Yudhishthira warns that Uttara must come in without Vrihannala.

scenes.B04C066S01: Virata returns, hears that Uttara has gone out with a eunuch as driver, sends troops, and receives news of the victory.
scenes.B04C066S02: Virata calls for dice, Kanka reluctantly agrees to play, and Virata grows angry at Kanka's praise of Vrihannala.
scenes.B04C066S03: Virata strikes Yudhishthira with a die, Draupadi catches the blood, and Yudhishthira asks that Uttara enter alone.
