shots.B04C066S01H01: Virata enters his city in triumph with the four Pandavas, sits on his throne, and receives his subjects. He asks where Uttara has gone, and the women reply that the prince went out alone with Vrihannala to face the six great Kuru warriors.
shots.B04C066S01H02: Virata grieves and sends horses, elephants, chariots and foot-soldiers after his son, saying that a prince with a eunuch as driver is surely dead.
shots.B04C066S01H03: Yudhishthira smiles and says that if Vrihannala is the driver, the Kurus will never take the cattle and Uttara will prevail against all the lords of the earth.
shots.B04C066S01H04: The messengers arrive and report the Kuru defeat, the recovered cattle and Uttara's safe return. Yudhishthira says he is not surprised, since Vrihannala is the driver.
shots.B04C066S01H05: Virata is overjoyed and orders the highways decorated and the gods honoured, and sends out musicians and courtesans to meet his son, with proclamations at the crossroads.
shots.B04C066S02H01: The citizens, with music and hymns, go out to welcome Uttara. Virata calls for the dice, and Kanka says a man whose heart is full of joy should not gamble with a cunning player, but agrees to play if the king wishes.
shots.B04C066S02H02: Virata offers to wager his cows, women and gold, and Kanka warns that gambling brings many evils and recalls how Yudhishthira lost his kingdom at dice.
shots.B04C066S02H03: Virata says his son has defeated the Kurus. Yudhishthira answers that a warrior with Vrihannala as driver will surely conquer.
shots.B04C066S02H04: Virata grows angry, calling Kanka a Brahmana who compares a eunuch with his son, and warns him not to say it again.
shots.B04C066S02H05: Yudhishthira insists that no one in the world can match Vrihannala, and Virata replies that without punishment no one would practise virtue.
shots.B04C066S03H01: Virata strikes Yudhishthira's face with a die and his nose bleeds. Draupadi catches the blood in a golden vessel. Uttara arrives at the gate, and Yudhishthira warns the porter that Uttara must enter alone, since Vrihannala would avenge any bloodshed of Yudhishthira's.

B04C067.summary: Uttara enters and finds Kanka bleeding and tended by Draupadi, and asks his father who struck him. Virata admits the blow, and Uttara begs him to make amends before a Brahmana's curse destroys him. Kanka forgives the king, and once the bleeding stops Vrihannala enters the court. Virata praises his son for defeating the greatest Kuru warriors.

scenes.B04C067S01: Uttara finds Kanka bleeding, Virata admits the blow, Kanka forgives him, and Virata praises his son.

shots.B04C067S01H01: Uttara bows to his father and sees Kanka covered in blood, seated at the edge of the court and attended by the Sairindhri. He asks in alarm who struck him.
shots.B04C067S01H02: Virata says he struck the crooked Brahmana, who deserved more, for praising a person of the third sex while Virata was praising his son.
shots.B04C067S01H03: Uttara warns his father that he must appease Kanka before a Brahmana's curse consumes him.
shots.B04C067S01H04: Kanka says he has long forgiven the blow. Had his blood fallen to the ground, the king and his kingdom would have been destroyed, but he does not blame him, since the powerful often act without reason.
shots.B04C067S01H05: When the bleeding stops, Vrihannala enters and salutes the king and Kanka. Virata praises Uttara as a true son, asks how he could have faced Karna, Bhishma, Drona, Ashvatthaman and Duryodhana, and says he has routed the foe and taken back the kine like prey snatched from a tiger.

B04C068.summary: Uttara tells his father that he did not win the battle himself, but that a celestial youth took the reins, drove him against the Kurus, and routed the great warriors, then challenged Duryodhana to fight. Virata asks to honour the youth who saved his cattle, but Uttara says the youth vanished and may return. Virata remains ignorant of Arjuna's identity, and Arjuna presents the new garments he has brought to Virata's daughter, delighting her and Uttara.

scenes.B04C068S01: Uttara credits the victory to a celestial youth, Virata asks to honour him, and Arjuna gives the garments to Virata's daughter.

shots.B04C068S01H01: Uttara says the cattle were not recovered by him, but by a celestial youth who stopped him from fleeing, took the reins, and challenged Duryodhana to fight for sovereignty or death.
shots.B04C068S01H02: Uttara describes how the youth routed Kripa, Drona, Ashvatthaman, Karna and Bhishma, stripped the Kuru warriors of their garments, and defeated six great car-warriors alone.
shots.B04C068S01H03: Virata asks to see the celestial youth who saved his wealth, so that he may honour him.
shots.B04C068S01H04: Uttara says the youth disappeared after the battle and will probably show himself in a day or two.
shots.B04C068S01H05: Virata does not recognize that the youth is living in his palace in disguise. Arjuna presents the costly garments he has brought to Virata's daughter, and Uttara and his sister are delighted.

B04C069.summary: On the third day after the vow was completed, the five Pandavas enter Virata's council hall, bathed and finely dressed, and take their places on royal thrones. Virata, angry to see the dice-player Kanka seated like a king, demands to know how he dares. Arjuna answers with a long, teasing speech praising Yudhishthira's virtue, learning, power and wealth, and argues that he deserves the royal seat.

scenes.B04C069S01: The Pandavas take royal seats in Virata's council, Virata rebukes Kanka, and Arjuna answers with praise of Yudhishthira.

shots.B04C069S01H01: On the third day, the five Pandavas enter the palace dressed in white and jewels, and sit on royal thrones in the council hall, shining like sacrificial fires. Virata, filled with anger, rebukes Kanka for sitting in royal seat and dress as though he were a courtier who was once a dice-player.
shots.B04C069S01H02: Arjuna answers with a jesting speech, saying that Kanka deserves the seat of Indra. He praises Yudhishthira's learning, austerity, generosity, wealth, followers and command over the kings, and asks whether such a king does not deserve a royal seat.

B04C070.summary: Virata asks which of the men is which, and Arjuna names each brother and Draupadi, recalling their deeds in the hidden year. Uttara describes the brothers' appearance and tells of Arjuna's great feats in the battle. Virata, feeling guilty for having wronged Yudhishthira, offers his daughter, also named Uttara, to Arjuna, and then begs forgiveness and makes an alliance with the Pandavas, offering Yudhishthira his kingdom, which Arjuna accepts on her behalf.

scenes.B04C070S01: Virata asks who the men are, Arjuna and Uttara identify the brothers and Draupadi and recount Arjuna's feats, and Virata offers his daughter to Arjuna.
scenes.B04C070S02: Uttara and Virata ask the Pandavas' forgiveness, and Virata makes an alliance and offers his kingdom, which Arjuna accepts for his daughter-in-law.

shots.B04C070S01H01: Virata asks which of the men is Yudhishthira, which Arjuna, Bhima, Nakula and Sahadeva, and where the famous Draupadi is, since no one has heard of them since their defeat at dice.
shots.B04C070S01H02: Arjuna names Vallava as Bhima, and recounts his feats such as slaying Rakshasas and killing the Kichakas. He names Nakula as the horse-keeper and Sahadeva as the cowherd, identifies Draupadi as the Sairindhri, and says they lived secretly in the king's house like infants in a womb.
shots.B04C070S01H03: Uttara points out Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, the twins and Krishna by their looks and bearing, describing each in turn.
shots.B04C070S01H04: Uttara describes Arjuna's feats: he slew warriors in the chariot-throng, killed a huge elephant with a single arrow, recovered the kine, deafened him with his conch, and vanquished Bhishma, Drona and Duryodhana.
shots.B04C070S01H05: Virata, feeling he has wronged Yudhishthira, says it is time to propitiate the Pandavas, and offers to give his daughter Uttara to Arjuna.
shots.B04C070S02H01: Uttara says the time has come to worship the illustrious sons of Pandu.
shots.B04C070S02H02: Virata credits Bhima with rescuing him and Arjuna with recovering the cattle, asks the Pandavas to forgive any offence, and says Yudhishthira is virtuous.
shots.B04C070S02H03: Virata makes an alliance, offers his kingdom, treasury and capital to Yudhishthira, embraces the brothers and asks Arjuna to take Uttara's hand. Arjuna, with Yudhishthira's approval, accepts her as a daughter-in-law.

B04C071.summary: Virata offers his daughter to Arjuna, and Arjuna accepts her as a daughter-in-law for his son Abhimanyu, insisting that he lived with her in the palace without impropriety. The allies gather at Upaplavya, the wedding is celebrated with gifts and dowry, and Virata offers the Pandavas his kingdom and treasure. The section and the Virata Parva close here, and the chapter is followed by the translator's footnotes and the Project Gutenberg license text.

scenes.B04C071S01: Virata offers his daughter, Arjuna accepts her for his son, the allies gather and the wedding is celebrated, and the Virata Parva ends.

shots.B04C071S01H01: Virata asks why Arjuna will not take his daughter as a wife.
shots.B04C071S01H02: Arjuna says he saw the princess daily in the palace and lived with her for a year, so to remove any suspicion he accepts her as a daughter-in-law for his son Abhimanyu, the favoured nephew of Krishna.
shots.B04C071S01H03: Virata praises Arjuna's words and leaves the next steps to him, saying that whoever has Arjuna as a son-in-law has all his desires fulfilled.
shots.B04C071S01H04: Yudhishthira agrees, and invitations go out to Krishna and the allies, who gather at Upaplavya with their troops. The wedding of Uttara and Abhimanyu is celebrated with dowry of horses, elephants and wealth, Virata offers his kingdom, Yudhishthira gives gifts to the Brahmanas, and the city holds a great festival.
shots.B04C071S01H05: A closing line marks the end of the Virata Parva.
shots.B04C071S02H02: Note 1 says that Nilakantha takes Brahma Vadini to mean one devoted to praising Krishna.
shots.B04C071S02H04: Note 2 says that a speech of Vaisampayana is omitted in some texts, and that including it in the third section would be a mistake.
shots.B04C071S03H01: Note 3 says that a verse beginning with 'Adushta' appears only in Bengal texts.
shots.B04C071S03H03: Note 4 says that a variant reading exists here, but the sense is the same.
shots.B04C071S03H05: Note 5 glosses a term as an independent female artisan working in another person's house, a gloss credited to Wilson.
shots.B04C071S04H02: Note 6 says some Bengal texts read a different word and that the Bengal form is wrong.
shots.B04C071S04H04: Note 7 discusses a very difficult verse about not divulging what happens in the king's presence, and the reading Nilakantha adopts.
shots.B04C071S05H01: Note 8 says the Bengal editions read an instrumental case, and the translator follows a manuscript reading in the genitive.
shots.B04C071S05H03: Note 9 identifies Mahishasura as the son of Rambhasura, a demon Durga fought for years, and notes the legend's place in the Markandeya Purana and Bengal's autumn festival.
shots.B04C071S05H05: Note 10 says Durga's name literally means one who rescues from difficulty.
shots.B04C071S06H02: Note 11 says Nilakantha explains kamachara in one sense, though elsewhere the word means something else.
shots.B04C071S06H04: Note 12 glosses the attack and defence words, and notes a variant that would mean cased in gauntlets.
shots.B04C071S07H01: Note 13 says Bhuti, Hri, Sri, Kirti and Kanti are the feminine forms of prosperity, modesty, beauty, fame and loveliness.
shots.B04C071S07H03: Note 14 explains that Draupadi wishes time to pass quickly, since in her misery she cannot wish it to stand still.
shots.B04C071S07H05: Note 15 glosses the phrase as meaning she from whom one is born.
shots.B04C071S08H02: Note 16 gives a variant phrase meaning an elephant lifting a vela fruit.
shots.B04C071S08H04: Note 17 says the word can mean kettle-drum or trumpet, and that trumpet suits the passage better.
shots.B04C071S09H01: A short gloss on Bhima's strength in his thighs appears here, apparently out of place.
shots.B04C071S09H03: Note 19 says Bhima's words mean that the Gandharvas always obey Draupadi, so their help only repays a debt.
shots.B04C071S09H05: Note 20 discusses the phrase krita-krita, which Nilakantha reads as success in a mission, and the translator reads it differently, since the same word recurs later.
shots.B04C071S10H02: Note 21 admits that a verse is very difficult and that the translator consulted friends, and says the meaning fits Bhishma's advice.
shots.B04C071S10H04: Note 22 explains a phrase as indicating the unobstructed completion of a sacrifice.
shots.B04C071S11H01: Note 23 says the word tirtha here means spies, not holy places.
shots.B04C071S11H03: Note 24 rejects Nilakantha's reading of satram as false disguise, and takes it to mean forest.
shots.B04C071S11H05: Note 25 says the verse is misprinted in most texts and explains which word readings the translator adopts.
shots.B04C071S12H02: Note 26 says bhagasas means each in its proper place, or according to their divisions.
shots.B04C071S12H04: Note 27 glosses kalyana-patalam as a covering of gold.
shots.B04C071S13H01: Note 28 identifies the named figure as one of Virata's generals.
shots.B04C071S13H03: Note 29 lists variant readings for two words in a verse.
shots.B04C071S13H05: Note 30 says some texts read Ghanabiva for Ghanarva, the latter being the better form.
shots.B04C071S14H02: Note 31 explains that a muhurta is not exactly forty-eight minutes here, since the moon would rise some time after sunset.
shots.B04C071S14H04: Note 32 gives Nilakantha's reading of the words of assurance Bhima speaks to Virata, and a possible variant.
shots.B04C071S15H01: Note 33 says the adjective Bhima-sankasas is explained with reference to Valmiki's simile.
shots.B04C071S15H03: Note 34 describes the Indian vina, with its bamboo neck, gourds, strings and frets, so the comparison can be understood.
